extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark designed to evaluate the temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs). MVBench covers 20 challenging video tasks that require temporal reasoning, ranging from perception to cognition, and cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. The benchmark is built by transforming static image tasks into dynamic video tasks using a novel static-to-dynamic method, and automatically converting public video annotations into multiple-choice QA format for evaluation. MVBench includes a robust video MLLM baseline, VideoChat2, which significantly outperforms existing models by over 15% on the benchmark.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.citeAs: MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos were collected from 11 public video benchmarks (STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, TVQA) covering diverse domains, scenes, and perspectives (first-person, third-person, indoor, outdoor). Videos were filtered based on temporal sensitivity (intermediate duration of 5s to 35s), question difficulty, and video diversity to ensure comprehensive evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public video benchmarks with high-quality annotations: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, TVQA
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were filtered to ensure temporal sensitivity (5s to 35s duration), question difficulty balancing, and video diversity. Short clips with negligible motion and long videos with overly complex contexts were excluded. For QA generation, annotations were converted into multiple-choice format using ChatGPT for question generation and template-based or LLM-based methods for answer options.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were automatically converted into multiple-choice QA format. Questions were generated based on task definitions using ChatGPT, and answer options were created either through template-based construction (directly from ground truth annotations) or LLM-based generation (e.g., for Unexpected Action tasks). Options were shuffled and balanced in length to prevent answer leakage.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: ChatGPT (for question generation and answer option creation), with manual oversight for quality control
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answer options were shuffled and balanced in length to ensure robustness. LLM was used to guarantee that options for a question were of similar and reasonable lengths, preventing longer options from being correct.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 200 multiple-choice QA pairs per temporal understanding task
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT, LLM-based question and answer generation
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and models are publicly available at https://github.com/OpenGVLab/Ask-Anything. Versioning information, maintainers, and deprecation policies are not explicitly stated in the paper.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to advance the evaluation of temporal understanding in Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), which is critical for applications requiring procedural activity understanding in real-world scenarios. The dataset emphasizes fairness and accuracy in evaluation by using ground-truth video annotations to avoid biased scoring of LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases may arise from the source datasets (e.g., CLEVRER for simulated environments, STAR for real-world indoor scenes). The static-to-dynamic transformation may introduce biases in task definitions. The paper acknowledges that current MLLMs struggle with localization and counting tasks, suggesting limitations in generalization.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) Difficulty in generalizing to localization and counting tasks due to lack of related tuning data. (2) Struggles with complex egocentric navigation and episode reasoning, indicating that visual information alone may not be sufficient. (3) Performance gaps in position-related tasks, where models perform similarly to random guessing. (4) Limited exposure to certain tasks (e.g., position, count, character) during instruction tuning may affect performance.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Benchmarking for Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs). The dataset is designed to evaluate temporal understanding capabilities, including perception, cognition, and reasoning in dynamic video contexts. Usage guidelines emphasize the benchmark's role in assessing models' ability to understand procedural activities and temporal evolution in videos.
